key_insight: In turbulent concentric annular pipe flow, passive heat transfer cannot be captured well by a simple linear near-wall temperature law; curvature and finite-Re effects produce a logarithmic wall behavior that depends strongly on radius ratio.
engineering_relevance: Design and heat-transfer correlations for curved annular ducts should include radius-ratio effects, even at high Reynolds numbers and low Prandtl numbers, to avoid systematic prediction errors.
method: Used stochastic one-dimensional turbulence (ODT) to resolve viscous, conductive, and turbulent advective transport along a representative radial coordinate.
Studied concentric annular pipe flow over an extended parameter range in radius ratio, including highly turbulent regimes.
Kept the model calibration fixed for Pr = 0.71 and 0.025 to test predictive heat-transfer scaling.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical boundary-layer profiles and ODT simulations that were compared across radius ratio and flow regime, then used to fit an extended Nusselt correlation.
watch_item: The heat-transfer correlation is calibrated for specific low/moderate Prandtl numbers, so applying it outside that range or ignoring curvature effects may reduce accuracy.
paper_title: Numerical Simulation of Turbulent Concentric Annular Pipe Flow using One-Dimensional Turbulence (ODT): Part 2: Heat Transfer
